messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm opening a PR to consolidate the function-calling + structured-output examples into one page. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321 :wave:

docs-bot: PR created by maya — added to 'docs' project, requested reviewers: elena, samir

elena: Nice! Quick ask — can we include a compact JSON schema example and one small fallback parsing paragraph? Those are the two things most users trip on.

samir: I can take the fallback parsing blurb. I have a 3-line snippet that shows a robust parse strategy (try JSON.parse, then fallback regex + safe-split).

maya: Perfect. Elena — can you handle the example snippets and SDK JS/py usage? Kevin said he can help with link-checks and CLI snippet testing.

elena: Yep. I'll add a minimal JS SDK example and a Python sync/async example. Plan: one canonical JSON schema, then two small SDK examples showing how to call and validate.

kevin: I'll run the link checker and also test the code samples locally. FYI I hit a mismatch in the model catalog link last week — I'll sweep for those.

maya: Samir — for the fallback paragraph, can you include an explicit note about nullable tool outputs and arrays being sometimes emitted as a string? We should show a quick pre-parse normalization step.

samir: Sure. Draft coming in a minute: 
```
# pseudo-code parse flow
try:
  parsed = json.loads(response)
except JSONDecodeError:
  # handle cases where LLM returns a stringified JSON inside another field
  raw = response.strip('"')
  parsed = json.loads(raw)
# finally, coerce single-item arrays to arrays if schema requires
```

elena: For the schema example I'm thinking this (tiny):
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "command": {"type": "string"},
    "params": {"type": "object"}
  },
  "required": ["command"]
}
```

maya: Love it. Two minor docs decisions: 1) call out that function names are case-sensitive and should match tool registry, 2) add a 'How to recover' bullet for common parse failures.

elena: Adding both. I'm going to also include a small 'test harness' snippet that runs an eval prompt against a few golden inputs so we can catch regressions.

kevin: Link fixes: I found three stale links in other pages while checking. I'll post a follow-up PR with redirects if needed.

maya: Timing — would be great to land this before end of sprint (Thu). Reviewers: please try to review within 24 hours. If you can't, flag here.

elena: I can review tomorrow morning PST.

samir: Reviewing tonight.

kevin: I'll do link checks after elena's edits so I don't get false positives.

maya: One more thing — let's add a tiny regression test to the docs CI that runs the example through the SDK snippet runner. Kevin, can you add that as a follow-up?

kevin: Yep, I'll add a CI job that runs the JS snippets and reports failures as part of docs build. Should be small.

maya: Awesome. Assigning tasks in the PR description. I'll merge once elena + samir sign off, and CI passes. Thanks y'all :tada:
